newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Consob suspends Refco Italia for 60 days.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Consob suspends Refco Italia for 60 days.

text.p: Italy's stock market regulator Consob said in a statement that it had suspended licensed broker Refco Italia Sim, in which Refco Inc of the U.S. has a 50 percent stake, for two months for a series of violations.
Refco Italia is alleged to have told clients it was authorised to act as a depositary for funds managed by third parties even though it was not authorised to do so.
The Consob statement added that Refco Italia was "structurally slanted towards the interests of the group to which it belongs."
This meant that, in effect, unauthorised foreigners were directly conducting brokerage in Italy through Refco Italia, Consob said.
Foreign organisations are not currently allowed to conduct broking in Italy, although they can put orders through a local licensed intermediary. Refco has 30 days to appeal the ruling.

A new law comes into force in Italy on Monday, known as the Eurosim law, authorising foreigners to buy and sell securities in Italy without having to go through a local broker, but regulations implementing the law have yet to be enacted.
